transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

I'm really struggling because I keep having these episodes where I eat massive amounts of food in a very short time. Once I start, I feel like I completely lose control and just can't stop myself. It's really taking a toll on me and I need help.
After these episodes of overeating, do you engage in any behaviors to try to prevent weight gain, such as self-induced vomiting, excessive exercise, or the use of laxatives?

Yes, I feel so guilty and panicked afterward that I force myself to throw up and sometimes misuse laxatives to get rid of the food. I also try to fast for a day or two and force myself to exercise for hours until I'm completely exhausted. I just feel this desperate need to do whatever it takes to prevent gaining weight.

latest_inference.note: Previously the candidates were [Binge-Eating Disorder, Bulimia Nervosa]. The patient explicitly confirmed the use of compensatory behaviors (self-induced vomiting, laxative misuse, fasting, and excessive exercise) to prevent weight gain following episodes of binge eating. This diagnostic criteria rules out Binge-Eating Disorder and strongly points to Bulimia Nervosa.
